question.prompt: On average, for every \(4\) sports cars sold at the local car dealership, \(7\) sedans are sold. The dealership predicts that it will sell \(28\) sports cars next month. How many sedans does it expect to sell?

solutions.explanation:
The prediction keeps the same ratio of \(7\) sedans for every \(4\) sports cars. Since
\[
28\div4=7,
\]
the sports-car quantity is multiplied by \(7\). Multiply the sedan quantity by the same factor:
\[
7\times7=49.
\]
The dealership expects to sell \(\boxed{49}\) sedans, choice D.
solutions.title: Scale both quantities equally
